title: Options and their arm documents for the Arazzo catalogue
description: Lives at `catalogue/capabilities.yaml`. Each option is behaviour the released text leaves to the implementation, citing the sentence that leaves it. Its arms are keyed by the token a statement's `options` list selects one with, and each names the documents, by document id, that test it. The documents of every arm the statement does not select are skipped with `option-not-selected`, and a surface element counts as covered when every arm of its option covers it, or when the option's `decides` lists it, one arm asserts it, and every arm calls its operation. `validate` refuses an arm naming a document the catalogue does not hold, a document under two arms of one option, and a `decides` status no arm asserts or whose operation an arm does not call. `documents` states what a document needs before it runs, `floors` the workflow count each capability folder keeps, and `extension-only` the capability folders verified only over Veredictum's own extension routes.

documents.description: What a document needs from the statement before it runs, keyed by document id. `validate` refuses a key that names no document of the catalogue.

applies.description: The specification versions the document applies to, keyed by the component a statement's `spec_versions` declares a version of. Every workflow of the document is skipped version-out-of-range when the statement declares a version of a component outside its range; a component the statement does not declare decides nothing.

min.description: The first release the document applies to, inclusive.

max.description: The last release the document applies to, inclusive.

x-veredictum-cite.description: The released sentence that bounds the range, in the `arazzo-extensions` cite shape.

formats.description: The wire formats the server must serve or process for the document to run, in the statement's `tech_profiles` vocabulary. Every workflow of the document is skipped format-not-claimed when the statement's its-rest profile does not list one of them. A document that tests the refusal of a format needs nothing: it runs for a party that does not serve the format.

floors.description: The workflow count each capability folder keeps, keyed by folder name. `validate` refuses a folder without a floor, a floor naming no folder, and a folder holding fewer workflows than its floor; a test re-derives every floor from the catalogue, so a floor moves with the folder it counts.

extension-only.description: The capability folders verified only over the routes of `catalogue/sources/veredictum-extensions.openapi.yaml`, which no openEHR OAS describes. `validate` refuses a listed folder with a step calling another source, and an unlisted folder whose every step calls that one.

x-veredictum-cite.description: The citation, in the `arazzo-extensions` cite shape.

decides.description: The response branches the arms are the mutually exclusive answers to: for each operation, the statuses a service answers with one arm or another, and the released sentence that makes them alternatives. A listed status counts as covered when one arm asserts it and every arm calls the operation; every other element needs every arm. No openEHR spec governs this, our own design.

x-veredictum-cite.description: The citation, in the `arazzo-extensions` cite shape.
